channel.title: Violations Watch: grave violations against children
channel.description: New incidents tagged with one of the six grave violations against children (UN Security Council resolution 1612). Open-source leads, not UN-verified cases.

item.title: Three Afghan migrants, a man, a woman and a young child, found shot dead near the Iran–Pakistan border in Saravan; rights group Haalvsh alleges Iranian forces shot them (KabulNow, Khaama Press)
item.description: Unverified lead (High priority). Bacheh-Rahi area, Kalagan district, Saravan County, Sistan and Baluchestan, Iran. Types: Killing of civilians, Executions. Alleged perpetrator: Iranian military or border forces (alleged by Haalvsh and its sources; Iranian authorities had not commented). Reported casualties: 3 killed. Grave violations against children: Killing and maiming. Disputed or caveats: Both outlets rely on Haalvsh and videos it published; not independently verified; child's age not given; no Iranian comment. 3 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-2743

item.title: Drone strike on a passenger bus near al-Thalatheen Street, west of Taiz city, kills three civilians, including a 10-year-old boy and his father, and critically injures one; government-side sources blame the Houthis (ANI, Al-Majhar)
item.description: Unverified lead (High priority). near al-Thalatheen Street, west of Taiz city, Yemen. Types: Air / drone / artillery strike, Killing of civilians. Alleged perpetrator: Houthis (per an al-Thawra hospital medical source and government agency Saba). Reported casualties: 3 killed, 1 injured. Grave violations against children: Killing and maiming. Disputed or caveats: Attribution comes from government-side sources only (Saba, al-Thawra hospital source, pro-government outlets); no Houthi comment. ANI mentions no bus but gives the same toll on the same day (3 killed incl. 10-year-old boy and father); ANI's injured figure of 3 includes separate shelling and sniper incidents. 3 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-2751
